verdict.rationale: Modal Sandboxes provide fresh, isolated, ephemeral containers for running untrusted agent code. The SDK also exposes network controls (block_network, CIDR and domain allowlists) that can wall a sandbox off from outside systems, so the core of safe testing is delivered by the product itself. However, the evidence never explicitly addresses keeping sandbox testing separate from production data: there is no documented test-versus-production environment separation or data-isolation guarantee, so coverage is only partial. missing for 10: explicit documentation of separating sandbox tests from production data or environments, guidance on data isolation for mounted volumes and secrets, independent or hands-on corroboration of the isolation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Spin up fresh, isolated sandboxes programmatically.
Programmatically scale secure, ephemeral environments for running untrusted code.
We execute the agent's code in a Modal Sandbox, which allows us to run arbitrary code in a safe environment.
secure containers for executing untrusted user or agent code
